headline: Nine days to the crossing and the taper is doing exactly its job. Legs banked, engine intact, strength quietly maintained. The quiet is the plan, not a warning.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: This is a taper reading, and it holds together cleanly. The running volume that surged over the last four weeks has now deliberately thinned, with the recent easy run confirming the legs are fresh rather than stale after the block's longest rest stretch. Strength has stayed live as light maintenance rather than tapering to nothing — a reasonable call this close to a 580 km self-supported effort. Steps remain genuinely high on active days, which matters more than usual right now: it keeps the legs ticking even as logged running drops off. Recovery and load metrics both read "quiet" — the strain figure has collapsed against the 28-day baseline, which in any other block would be a flag but here is precisely the intended shape. Nothing in this picture contradicts the taper story.
sections.trends: The 16-week arc shows a real build peaking in the recent four-week window, followed by a sharp intentional drawdown — a clean pre-event taper rather than a plateau or a stall. Year-to-date, the contrast with the same date last year is stark: this year's accumulated distance dwarfs it, which is the base that makes a 9-10 day crossing plausible in the first place. The shape makes sense: a genuine build, then a deliberate unloading right before the event, sitting inside an otherwise non-periodised year-round approach.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace has drifted marginally slower than the 30-day baseline, but this is within-block noise during a taper, not a fitness signal — the reference reading predates the heaviest training weeks, and freshness from unloading typically doesn't reflect in threshold numbers until the athlete tests fresh legs at speed again. For the crossing specifically, threshold pace is largely academic: the event is governed by durability and time-on-feet at aerobic effort, not by where the lactate turnpoint sits. The aerobic engine, as the recent controlled easy runs show, is intact.
sections.zones: The recent session mix is exactly what a taper wants: predominantly Z1-Z2 easy running with the one sharp tempo effort banked well before the quiet stretch — that session's meaningful Z3/Z4 time was the last real intensity injection, and correctly had no follow-up. Everything since has sat low and controlled with minimal grey-zone drift. For an ultra taper this is the right distribution: no ambiguity, no accidental moderate-hard sessions eating into recovery. The strength sessions similarly sit almost entirely in Z1, consistent with maintenance rather than a training stimulus.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength HR reads low and steady across recent sessions, sitting mostly in Z1 with brief Z2 excursions — consistent with maintenance-intensity functional work rather than anything taxing, which is appropriate this close to departure. Note that the most recent strength sessions logged no HR at all, so there's less to read there, but the character across the block has been uniformly light. Nothing in the sensor-source picture is worth flagging.
sections.calendar: The calendar shows the block's longest quiet running stretch resolving into a single easy run — a deliberate rhythm rather than a lapse, with strength stitched through the gaps to keep frequency alive. The running streak sits at its personal best length, which is worth noting: consistency has been the backbone of this build, and the taper hasn't broken it. Expect the pattern to fragment further as travel and packing logistics ramp; that's logistics, not deconditioning.
sections.personal_bests: None of the speed PBs are in play here — the taper and event focus point entirely away from short-distance sharpness right now. The relevant "best" over the next fortnight is a durability one: the crossing itself dwarfs the current longest logged effort in both distance and duration. That's the frontier being tested, and it won't show up on this list until after.

watch_items: Watch how the legs handle the transition from short controlled runs to sustained daily time-on-feet once the crossing starts — the first two or three days are the real durability audit.
Note whether strength drops fully to zero in the final pre-travel days or holds one more light session; either is fine, just track which way it breaks.
Keep steps from collapsing to cold rest-day zeros as logistics intensify, so the legs stay warm into departure.
Read sleep purely as context through the packing-and-travel window, not as a readiness signal.
